title: A supercheap Android phone with looks to spare
author: David Pierce

recommendations.name: The CMF Phone 1
recommendations.blurb: A nice-looking, long-lasting Android phone for $200? With an OLED screen and interchangeable backplates and a bunch of really cool accessories, one of which is a kickstand? Yes. Please. In orange, of course.

recommendations.name: The Samsung Galaxy Ring
recommendations.blurb: I’m still a fan of Samsung’s Fold and Flip phones, even though the new models are very same-y and even more expensive. But I’m most excited about the Galaxy Ring, which seems to have pretty much nailed the smart ring hardware — and even has some interesting ideas about gesture control.

recommendations.name: The Diggnation Reunion Part 1
recommendations.blurb: “ The Diggnation Reunion Part 1.” If you’re a tech lover of a certain age, there’s a strong chance you grew up watching Kevin Rose and Alex Albrecht drink and make jokes about tech while sitting on a couch. Watching the guys get back together was a delightful blast from the past.

recommendations.name: Delta 1.6
recommendations.blurb: Delta’s game emulation is on the iPad! I’m actually not sure how much I’ll use this given how much of my retro gaming is on an iPhone with a Backbone controller. But this update, with a bigger screen and support for multiple games at once, does sound pretty great.

recommendations.name: Amazon’s new Echo Spot
recommendations.blurb: To me, this is the exact right balance of things for an Alexa speaker. It’s small, it’s $45 (for now), it has a touchscreen but no camera, and it’s the right size for a nightstand. I keep promising to leave my phone out of my bedroom, and maybe this’ll replace it.

recommendations.name: Sunny
recommendations.blurb: A woman loses her husband but gets a robot from his tech company to help her through it. Strangeness ensues. Such a good premise! And by all accounts, this show continues Apple TV Plus’ run of great sci-fi stuff. I’ll definitely catch up before episode 3 drops on Wednesday.

recommendations.name: Openvibe
recommendations.blurb: Bluesky, Mastodon, Threads, and Nostr, all in one timeline in one app. This is basically a clever hack, not the interconnected social universe of my dreams, but it’s a pretty good hack! And I like that it basically hides which network people are using; it’s just people, in a timeline.

recommendations.name: Pestle
recommendations.blurb: I love a good recipe app. I mostly use Crouton and Mela, but Pestle’s new ability to import recipes from Instagram Reels is pretty awesome. Just drop in the link, give it a name, and it’ll turn a video into a bunch of ingredients and steps.

recommendations.name: iPhone 13 Mini
recommendations.blurb: The phone: iPhone 13 Mini.

recommendations.name: Flightradar24
recommendations.blurb: I feel like a wizard just pointing Flightradar24 at the sky or MarineTraffic at the sea to see where ships and planes are coming from and going to.

recommendations.name: MarineTraffic
recommendations.blurb: I feel like a wizard just pointing Flightradar24 at the sky or MarineTraffic at the sea to see where ships and planes are coming from and going to.

recommendations.name: CloudBeats
recommendations.blurb: CloudBeats: Essential for listening to podcast drafts while running and walking around; with Shell Game in production, I’m on this thing for hours a day sometimes.

recommendations.name: Libby
recommendations.blurb: Libby: Any New Yorker who doesn’t have it is missing out.

recommendations.name: Instapaper
recommendations.blurb: Instapaper: Anyone else still using Instapaper out there?

recommendations.name: Mossin’ Annie
recommendations.blurb: Websites on how to maintain it and its incredible properties, moss gurus (e.g., Mossin’ Annie ).

recommendations.name: Charley Crockett album
recommendations.blurb: The new Charley Crockett album.

recommendations.name: The Braindead Megaphone
recommendations.blurb: Currently revisiting The Braindead Megaphone, George Saunders’ essay collection, parts of which feel very Shell Game -relevant to me.

recommendations.name: Taskmaster
recommendations.blurb: My sister-in-law, who is 50x more culturally aware than I, turned us on to this British comic game show, Taskmaster.

recommendations.name: Slick Inbox
recommendations.blurb: I just wanted to share an app that (and it is a shock for me) no one knows about. It’s called Slick Inbox. The idea is very simple: it allows you to create your own inbox only for newsletters. I hate reading newsletters in my personal Gmail box, and this is a very convenient solution to my problem.

recommendations.name: Supacell
recommendations.blurb: I just binged all six episodes of Netflix’s Supacell. It’s like Heroes but grimier, set in South London, with an almost entirely Black cast and made by Rapman. It’s one of the best things I’ve seen this year and such a fresh show in a genre that is basically monopolized by Marvel.

recommendations.name: The Singularity is Nearer
recommendations.blurb: Currently reading The Singularity is Nearer by Ray Kurzweil. We are lucky to see human evolution in real time.

recommendations.name: Underdog Fantasy
recommendations.blurb: Best Ball drafts on Underdog Fantasy. What was once a niche version of fantasy football is now an (absurdly?) popular sports betting format where players draft an entire team within an hour or less and then compete against strangers.

recommendations.name: VR Exercise Tracker
recommendations.blurb: Using the VR Exercise Tracker app created by the VR Health Institute. They use science-backed measurement of VR activity to help you measure your VR workouts. Connects with Apple Watch and other Bluetooth fitness devices.

recommendations.name: Dungeons & Daddies
recommendations.blurb: As a new dad, Dungeons & Daddies resonates with me in a special way. This (self-described non-BDSM) podcast puts a hilarious twist on D&D, following four dads navigating a fantastical realm to rescue their lost sons.

recommendations.name: Boox Go 10.3
recommendations.blurb: Just bought a Boox Go 10.3 E Ink tablet and am really enjoying it. Very slim, nicely designed, no front light, and fairly great to write on when needed. It’s meant more as a competitor to the Remarkable 2 (i.e., a note-taking device), but I’m enjoying it for reading articles via Omnivore.

recommendations.name: Deep Work
recommendations.blurb: I’ve recently started reading a book called Deep Work by Cal Newport on the merits of dedicating time to focus on a task with minimal distractions.

recommendations.name: Apple PenLite: The iPad Before the iPad
recommendations.blurb: Apple PenLite: The iPad Before the iPad.” I have been watching Colin Holter’s channel for a few years now and really love his stuff, but this video is really something different for him. He interviewed several former Apple employees, and I thought it was really well done.

recommendations.name: Every Frame a Painting
recommendations.blurb: I sincerely believe that “ Every Frame a Painting ” is the best YouTube series of all time.

recommendations.name: Edgar Wright - How to Do Visual Comedy
recommendations.blurb: If you haven’t watched them, watch all of them. (If you only watch one, watch this one on Edgar Wright.

recommendations.name: David Fincher - And the Other Way is Wrong
recommendations.blurb: Or this one on David Fincher.

recommendations.name: the sound of Marvel movies
recommendations.blurb: Or this one on the sound of Marvel movies.

recommendations.name: The Second (2024) — A Limited Series Trailer
recommendations.blurb: Just watch them all!) So when the channel dropped its first video in seven years — a short trailer for a new limited series and short film — I immediately started refreshing the page every 10 minutes and rewatching every single thing on the channel all over again.
